chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Why the Decca tunes had already been recorded with Cugat
summary: The numbers were little-known Cuban publications, and restrictions made repeat recordings hard.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I notice that a lot of recordings that the Machito orchestra made when it backed-up Miguelito, for those Decca recordings, many of them had already been recorded with Cugat. Was this done on purpose? Was this Miguelito's way of getting back at Cugat by doing these things with your band?
No, because in those days there was, on account
that wasn't published by American publisher, it was practically unknown numbers that was published by Cubans.
I see. He did "Eco", "El Botellero", "Letargo", all these things......
......but he had done most of them already with Cugat.
Yes. On those days there was many restrictions..
.....and it became a battle, you know, you recorded one number and you need another five years in order to do it again or whatever, it really was a lot of hassle to get through.
